blocks.name: One recording from a quantum chip, read by two programs, gives two different error counts.
A qubit's state starts to smear within a thousandth of a blink.

sections.h: 2. The cure costs what it protects

blocks.name: The chip never looks at its qubits. It asks questions, and the answers light up.
All that leaves a quantum chip is a film of lights, and many different errors make the same lights.

sections.h: 5. The decoder, and the one mistake that matters
6. Where the standard method goes wrong

blocks.name: The standard program misses the answer that can happen in two ways.

sections.h: 7. The result that started us off

blocks.name: On Google's chip, each step to a bigger grid halved the errors.
Our small network passed the standard program one grid bigger only at the end of a run nearly four times longer, and still trailed the better free program.
What we can answer, and what is still open.
